summary_paragraph: A 59-year-old woman with end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis and advanced HIV was admitted for worsening right leg swelling following placement of a right femoral dialysis catheter. Imaging could not fully exclude a deep vein thrombosis due to catheter obstruction of the venous view, so she was treated with a heparin drip followed by warfarin. Her swelling resolved after dialysis and anticoagulation. She developed conjunctivitis with periorbital swelling, likely related to her history of herpes zoster, and was treated with valacyclovir and topical antibiotics, with significant improvement. Chest discomfort was attributed to esophagitis and resolved with fluconazole. She remained on her HAART regimen and prophylactic antibiotics. She was discharged home on warfarin, with instructions to complete her antiviral eye treatment and continue close monitoring of INR at dialysis.
problems: Other complications due to renal dialysis device, implant, and graft
